_comment: Knowledge Q/A pairs kept in sync by hand with Sources/AROAsk/KnowledgeBase.swift, so the aro_knowledge tool and the trained model give the same answers.

pairs.instruction: How do I fix "Event X is emitted but no handler exists"?
pairs.output: First search EVERY .aro file in the application for a feature set with business activity `X Handler` — ARO has no imports, all files are compiled together, and handlers often live in their own file. If one exists anywhere, change nothing: the warning is stale. Only if none exists, append `(Handle X: X Handler) { Extract the <field> from the <event: field>. ... Return an <OK: status> for the <handled>. }` extracting exactly the fields the Emit passes. Never add a second handler for the same event.

pairs.instruction: How do I fix "Variable v is defined but never used"?
pairs.output: Verify it first: loop bounds (`for <i> from 0 to <v>`), `when` guards, `${<v>}` interpolations and qualifier bases are all reads. If <v> is read anywhere, the report is wrong — change nothing. If it is genuinely unread, delete only the binding statement; if that statement is the sole content of a `case` or loop block, remove the enclosing block with it, because an empty block does not parse.

pairs.instruction: Can I invent a Compute qualifier if none fits?
pairs.output: No. The qualifier namespace is closed: built-ins, plugin qualifiers (handle.name), chains (a|b), or date offsets (-7d). An unknown name is a compile error. Sorting and reversing are actions (`Sort the <s> for the <x>.`), element access is an Extract (`Extract the <f: first> from the <x>.`), and a result type uses `as` (`Compute the <n> as Float from <s>.`).

pairs.instruction: Is spacing like `the<name>` or `<a>< <b>` a syntax error in ARO?
pairs.output: No. Spacing inside statements is not significant: `the<name>` equals `the <name>`, and `<a>< <b>` is the comparison `<a> < <b>` written tightly. When repairing a file, copy such lines byte-for-byte — "tidying" them is how repairs introduce errors.
